correctness.rationale: The proof partitions every cyclic rotation by maximal circular source run, first-run residual length, and whether the next distinct symbol is lower or higher. Comparisons of first different symbols fix group and residual order, and lex order of continued periodic tails is preserved under positive letter-wise powers. At each integer boundary multiple h_a q the last column spells the fixed word B_{a,epsilon}(q); in all intervening positions it consists of a positive string of a, of length (h_a-1)R_{a,epsilon}(q). The complete BWT decomposition follows by accounting for every position exactly once, including circular boundaries and equal rotations; replacing positive monochromatic lengths cannot change run heads. The monochromatic case is immediate. The embedded stand-alone checker independently confirms the whole BWT in 38,792 exhaustive expanded cases and 220 separate suffix-doubling cases, but these finite calculations are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: BWT run count and ordered run structure directly measure the clustered output of a central text-indexing transform. Here the entire cyclic BWT under arbitrary independently letter-wise-powered input is characterized, showing parameter rigidity at the sharp natural threshold h_a=2. This is an unbounded structural theorem about an established compression invariant, stronger than monotonicity and beyond an isolated finite table; it could simplify analysis of BWT indices under homopolymer or symbol-stuttering preprocessing. It does not assert invariant run lengths or sentinel-BWT behavior.
